sections.h2: What is the Florida homestead exemption worth to an owner?
sections.html:
It removes up to $50,000 of a home's assessed value from taxation, in two layers. The Department of Revenue explains that the first $25,000 applies to every tax on the property, school taxes included, while a second layer of up to $25,000 reaches only the assessed value above $50,000 and excludes school taxes (Florida Department of Revenue, homestead guide).

The second layer is indexed. Each January 1 the amount rises by the percentage change in the consumer price index when that change is positive, and it stays put when the change is negative. The department's table uses 2024 as its base year, so ask the county property appraiser for the figure on your current bill.

An exemption is not a refund. It lowers the taxable base, and the property still pays whatever millage the school board, county, city and special districts levy on what is left.

sections.h2: Who qualifies, and what can cost an owner the exemption?
sections.html:
An owner qualifies by holding title on January 1 and making the home a permanent residence by that date. A person can claim only one permanent residence, and the claim ends if the facts change.

The state's guide lists the main ways to lose it:

  • The unit is rented out.
  • The home stops being the owner's permanent residence.
  • The owner stops being a Florida permanent resident.

One carve-out sits in the veteran materials. A servicemember may rent out the homestead without abandoning the exemption under s. 196.061 (Department of Revenue, veterans and servicemember exemptions). Anyone else who moves out should tell the property appraiser rather than let a stale exemption sit on the roll.

sections.h2: When and how do I apply for homestead in Florida?
sections.html:
File Form DR-501 with the county property appraiser by March 1 of the tax year. The same March 1 date governs most exemptions and agricultural classifications, and the state calendar sets it as the filing deadline for them (Florida Department of Revenue, taxpayer calendar).

If a denial letter arrives, the clock is short. A petition to the value adjustment board must be filed 30 days after the denial letter was mailed. A challenge to the assessed value itself runs on a different track: a petition (one of the DR-486 forms) goes to the clerk of the court within 25 days of the August Notice of Proposed Property Taxes.

Because the appraiser decides eligibility and the tax collector sends the bill, a seller who is unsure which office handles a question should call the appraiser first.

sections.h2: What does Save Our Homes do for a long-time owner?
sections.html:
Save Our Homes limits how fast a homestead's assessed value can climb. After the first year of homestead and a just-value assessment, the yearly increase cannot exceed the lower of 3 percent or the change in the consumer price index, and assessed value never rises above just value (Florida Department of Revenue, assessment limitation guide).

The department's cap chart, revised January 2026, prints these figures:

Source: Florida Department of Revenue, Save Our Homes cap chart. The 2024 row shows how the 3 percent ceiling works when inflation runs above it.

Non-homestead property has its own limit: assessed value can rise no more than 10 percent a year, per the same department calendar page.

sections.h2: What happens to the exemption and the cap when I sell?
sections.html:
A sale resets the cap. Any sale, foreclosure or transfer of legal or beneficial title is a change of ownership, and the property goes back to just value the following January 1. The department lists exceptions, including transfers between spouses and certain transfers at death.

The next owner may therefore see a bigger bill than the one you paid, so a house that looks cheap to carry can cost a buyer far more. Your own exemption does not travel with the house. The buyer applies for a new one if the home becomes their permanent residence by January 1, again by March 1.

A seller who closes after the January 1 assessment date still carries that year's exemption status on the roll. The tax bill arrives in November, and the allocation between buyer and seller is a closing matter. The purchase contract decides who bears which share, so read that clause before signing.

sections.h2: Can I take my Save Our Homes savings to the next house?
sections.html:
Yes, through portability, if you act on time. You must establish the new homestead within three years of January 1 of the year the old homestead was abandoned, which is not the same as three years after the sale date. File Form DR-501T together with the DR-501 by March 1 (Department of Revenue assessment guide).

The statute reduces the new home's assessed value by the lesser of $500,000 or the gap between the old home's just and assessed values (s. 193.155(8)). The statute page also notes that ch. 2026-239 amendments first apply to the 2027 tax roll, so a seller planning a move should ask the property appraiser which version covers their year (Florida Statutes, s. 193.155).

sections.h2: Are there extra benefits for seniors, veterans and disabled owners?
sections.html:
Yes, and they sit on top of the basic exemption. A county or city may adopt additional exemptions, so availability depends on where the home is.

  • Age 65 or older: an ordinance may add up to $50,000 for owners whose household income is within the limit, which started at $20,000 and is adjusted yearly by CPI (s. 196.075(2)).
  • Age 65 or older with 25 years of permanent residence and just value under $250,000: an ordinance may exempt an amount equal to assessed value, subject to the income limit.
  • Veterans 65 or older with a permanent service-connected disability: a homestead discount equal to the VA disability percentage, which carries to an unremarried surviving spouse (s. 196.082).
  • Disabled ex-servicemembers rated 10 percent or more: a $5,000 reduction in assessed value (ss. 196.081, 196.091).
  • Total and permanent service-connected disability: possible total exemption on the homestead.

The Department of Revenue describes these in its senior and veteran guides (seniors, veterans). Local ordinances vary, so confirm the income limit and the adopting body with the appraiser.

sections.h2: Can I defer the tax instead of paying it?
sections.html:
Homestead owners can defer part of the bill. File Form DR-570 with the tax collector by March 31 following the assessment year. The deferral covers tax above 5 percent of the prior year's household income, and all of it if household income is under $10,000. A permanent resident aged 65 or older may defer the portion above 3 percent of household income.

Bills go out in November with an early-payment discount of 4 percent in November, 3 percent in December, 2 percent in January and 1 percent in February. Unpaid tax turns delinquent April 1, and certificates are sold by June 1 (Department of Revenue calendar). If a deferral is recorded against the home, the tax collector can state what it will take to clear it before you list.

sections.h2: What should a seller with a homestead check before listing?
sections.html:
Start with the property appraiser's record for the parcel. It shows the assessed value, the just value and whether the exemption is active, and the gap between the last two is the amount Save Our Homes has shielded from tax.

  • Whether the March 1 application was accepted for the current year.
  • Whether any senior, veteran or disability exemption is attached, since a buyer will not inherit it.
  • Whether a tax deferral under Form DR-570 is recorded.
  • Whether you plan to port the benefit, which starts a three year clock.

Bring the answers to the closing agent. A buyer who intends to live in the house must reapply, and a buyer who plans to rent it will not qualify at all while it is rented.

faqs.q: When must a Florida homestead claim be filed?
faqs.a: March 1 of the tax year, filed with the county property appraiser on Form DR-501. You must also have made the home your permanent residence by January 1. A denial goes to the value adjustment board, and that petition has a 30 day window running from the mailing of the denial letter.

faqs.q: How much is the Florida homestead exemption?
faqs.a: Up to $50,000 of assessed value. The first $25,000 applies to all taxes including school taxes, and the additional $25,000 applies only to value over $50,000 and only to non-school taxes. The additional amount is inflation indexed, so check the appraiser for the current figure.

faqs.q: Does the Save Our Homes cap transfer to the buyer?
faqs.a: No. A sale is a change of ownership, so the property is reassessed at just value the next January 1. Spouse transfers and certain transfers at death are listed exceptions.

faqs.q: Can I keep my cap if I buy another Florida home?
faqs.a: Possibly, through portability. Establish the new homestead within three years of January 1 of the year you abandoned the old one and file Form DR-501T with the DR-501 by March 1. The reduction is limited to the lesser of $500,000 or the old home's just-minus-assessed gap.

faqs.q: What happens if I rent out my homestead?
faqs.a: Renting the unit costs the exemption, as does ceasing to live there or leaving Florida as a permanent resident. A servicemember is the stated exception and may rent the homestead under s. 196.061 without abandoning it.
